h1: Trade licence and shop registration steps for a brewpub
title: Trade Licence and Shop Registration | Craft Beer School
desc: The trade licence, shops and establishments registration and other local permits a brewpub needs, in the order to apply for them.
teaser: The excise licence gets all the attention. The municipal trade licence is the one that quietly stops a launch.
standfirst: Every brewpub in India needs a stack of local registrations alongside its excise licence. Each comes from a different office and some need the others first. Here is how the trade licence and shop registration fit into that stack.
sections:
The trade licence comes from your municipal corporation or local body. It permits a specific trade at a specific address and confirms the business meets local health and safety rules. For a brewpub with a kitchen and bar, it may be a health or eating house trade licence. The name and the department differ by city.

The shops and establishments registration is under your state's Shops and Establishments Act. It is mainly a labour law registration: it covers working hours, holidays, leave and conditions for staff. Most commercial premises with employees need it.

Both are separate from your excise licence. Both are often asked for as part of the excise application or renewal. Rules, fees and names vary by state and city and change, so check the current process with your local body or a licensing consultant.

Local permits feed into each other. A typical sequence looks like this, though your state may differ:

  1. Company or firm registration, PAN and GST registration.
  2. Registered lease or ownership documents for the premises.
  3. Building approvals: sanctioned plan and occupancy certificate.
  4. Fire NOC, which usually needs the building documents.
  5. Shops and establishments registration.
  6. Municipal trade licence.
  7. FSSAI licence for the kitchen and food service.
  8. Pollution control consent where required.
  9. Excise licence for brewing and serving.

Many founders discover late that the trade licence needs the fire NOC, which needs a building document the landlord does not have. Our guide on the microbrewery licence shows where these sit in the full process.
What the trade licence application asks for

Expect to provide most of these, depending on the city:

  • Proof of ownership or a registered lease, plus landlord consent.
  • Property tax receipt for the premises.
  • Identity and address proof of the owners or directors.
  • Company registration documents.
  • Site plan or layout.
  • Fire NOC and, sometimes, pollution control consent.
  • Photographs of the premises.

Many cities now accept trade licence applications online. Inspections may still follow. Fees are usually set by trade type and area. The licence is often renewed every year. Put the renewal date in your calendar the day the licence arrives.

Registration is usually quick and online in most states. You will give business details, the number of employees, working hours and the manager's details. Some states have simplified or removed registration for very small establishments, while others require it from the first employee.

The registration brings obligations: displaying the certificate, keeping attendance and wage records and following state rules on hours and weekly holidays. Brewpubs open late should check the opening hours their state allows and any conditions for staff working at night, especially women staff, where states have specific rules.
Signage, music and the small permits

Around the trade licence sit smaller permits that can still cause trouble. Signboards may need advertisement permission from the local body. Playing recorded music in public usually needs licences from the relevant copyright societies. Weights and measures registration may apply to anything sold by quantity. Our guide on adding spirits and wine covers the bar side.

None of these is hard on its own. Together, there might be ten or more permits with different renewal dates.

Keep one sheet listing every licence and registration: name, issuing office, number, date issued, expiry, renewal fee and who is responsible. Keep scanned copies in one shared folder. Many brewpubs lose days of trade because one small licence lapsed quietly while the team was busy. A register like this is basic, but it is the difference between a smooth renewal season and a raid.

Treating compliance as a system, rather than a pile of papers, is part of running a brewpub as a business.
When a consultant earns their fee

Many founders handle the local registrations themselves and hire a licensing consultant for excise. That split often works. A consultant who knows your city can still save weeks on the trade licence and fire NOC, because they know which office handles what and which documents are commonly rejected. Ask any consultant for a written list of what they will file, the expected timeline and the government fees separately from their own fee.

Keep the originals and the login details for every online application yourself. When a consultant leaves or a relationship ends, those logins are what let you renew next year without starting again.

Phone or visit your local municipal office or check its website. Get the current trade licence checklist for a restaurant and bar in your ward. Compare it with the documents your landlord has already given you. Any gap is your first job this week.
faqs: Is a trade licence the same as an excise licence?
No. A trade licence comes from the municipal body and permits the business at that address. The excise licence covers brewing and selling alcohol. A brewpub needs both.
Does a brewpub need shops and establishments registration?
Usually yes, as it is a commercial premises with employees. The rules and any exemptions differ by state.
How often is a trade licence renewed?
Often every year, though it varies by city. Note the expiry date and renew before it lapses.
